paper_title: MathOdyssey Benchmarking Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills in Large   Language Models Using Odyssey Math Data
caption: Mathematical problems across educational levels. We curate and categorize problems by difficulty and subject area.
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the categorization of mathematical problems across different educational levels and subject areas. It is divided into 12 distinct slices representing various mathematical domains. The chart does not use a separate legend or place percentage labels inside the slices; instead, thin callout lines connect each segment to an external text label detailing the subject, educational level, percentage, and raw count in parentheses. Proceeding clockwise from the top, the slices represent: Statistics – University-level in light blue at 4.39% (17), Probability – University-level in cyan at 5.43% (21), Differential Equations – University-level in yellow-green at 3.62% (14), Calculus and Analysis – University-level in grey at 6.20% (24), Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level in pink at 6.46% (25), Pre-Calculus – High School in brown at 14.21% (55), Geometry – High School in light purple at 3.62% (14), Algebra – High School in salmon pink at 17.83% (69), Combinatorics – Olympiad-level in light green at 9.56% (37), Geometry – Olympiad-level in light orange at 6.46% (25), Number Theory – Olympiad-level in pale blue at 1.03% (4), and the largest slice, Algebra – Olympiad-level in dark blue at 21.19% (82). The segments do not appear to be ordered by descending or ascending size, and none of the slices are visually emphasized by being exploded, offset, or bolded.
